blocks.text: 1. Graph Traversal
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785447863304-804004816.png

Graph Construction closed by acknowledging that a well built graph still inherits every upstream extraction error. Graph Traversal, walking the constructed graph outward from a starting entity to find an answer, is the retrieval mechanism that actually puts a finished graph to use.
It follows edges from node to node, gathering the connected facts a query actually needs.
2. Starting From A Known Entity
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785447863304-562874598.png
As covered generally in Graph RAG as traversal replacing similarity search, a traversal begins at a specific node identified from the query itself.
Without a starting node, there is nothing for the traversal to walk outward from.
3. Following Edges By Relationship Type
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785447863305-325422651.png
As with edges representing relationships in Knowledge Graphs, a traversal follows only the specific relationship type relevant to the question.
It ignores every other edge attached to that same starting node.

blocks.content: {"headers":["Traversal behavior","What it does"],"rows":[["Following relevant edges","Follows only the relationship type the query needs"],["Ignoring irrelevant edges","Skips every other edge on the same node"]]}

blocks.text: 4. Single Hop Versus Multi-Hop Traversal
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785447863305-152115929.png
As with multi-hop questions benefiting most in Chain Of Thought, a single hop answers a direct question, while a chained question requires several hops in sequence.
Each hop's result determines which edge to follow next.
5. Traversal Depth Needs A Limit
As with agentic loops running too long in Agentic RAG, a graph with cycles can send an unbounded traversal walking in circles.
A maximum hop count keeps traversal bounded and predictable.

blocks.title: Note
blocks.content: A graph edge that loops back to an earlier visited node can trap an unbounded traversal in an endless cycle, the same runaway loop risk as an agentic loop running too long.

blocks.text: 6. Breadth First Versus Depth First Traversal

blocks.alt: Breadth First Versus Depth First Traversal
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785447863305-547732589.png
Breadth first traversal explores every neighbor before going deeper, while depth first follows one path as far as it goes first.
The right choice depends on whether the query needs breadth or a specific deep chain.

blocks.content: {"headers":["Traversal order","When it fits"],"rows":[["Breadth first","Query needs everything nearby the starting node"],["Depth first","Query needs one specific, deep relationship chain"]]}

blocks.text: 7. Traversal Can Return Multiple Paths
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785447863305-772480659.png
More than one path can connect a starting entity to an answer through different intermediate nodes.
Traversal often gathers several valid paths rather than assuming only one exists.
8. Traversal Results Need To Be Formatted For The Model
As with context injection, covered generally in Prompt Engineering for RAG, the raw graph paths a traversal finds still need to become readable text for the generation model.
Traversal output and prompt context are two different representations of the same facts.

blocks.title: Note
blocks.content: A traversal path stored internally as a chain of node and edge identifiers must be turned into a readable sentence like Falcon Cloud supplies Acme Corp before it can be injected into the prompt as usable context.

blocks.text: 9. Recognizing When Graph Traversal Is The Right Retrieval Mechanism

blocks.alt: Recognizing When Graph Traversal Is The Right Retrieval Mechanism
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785447863567-645123473.png
Questions requiring a specific relationship chain suit traversal well.
A question answerable by matching similar text, by contrast, suits plain vector retrieval better.

blocks.text: 11. Common Mistakes

items: Starting a traversal without first resolving a concrete starting node from the query.
Following every edge on a node instead of filtering to the relevant relationship type.
Running an unbounded traversal on a graph that contains cycles.
Passing raw graph paths directly into the prompt without formatting them as readable text.

blocks.text: 12. Key Takeaways

items: Graph traversal walks the constructed graph outward from a starting entity to find an answer.
A traversal begins at a specific node identified from the query itself.
Traversal follows only the relationship type relevant to the question, ignoring other edges.
A single hop answers a direct question; a chained question requires several hops in sequence.
A maximum hop count is needed to keep traversal bounded on graphs that contain cycles.
Breadth first traversal explores every neighbor first; depth first follows one path deeply.
More than one path can connect a starting entity to an answer, and traversal can gather several.
Raw graph paths still need to be formatted as readable text before they reach the prompt.
